messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: alert_cascade_check triggered x3 across prod-cluster-1 -> high error-rate + retry-loop. Pager sent to @ryan_oncall and @jane_sre. Link: https://telemetry/redwood/alerts/alert_cascade_check
ryan_oncall: reading it now. I see spike in grpc 500s from embeddings-service around 15:24 UTC. Starting a bridge. Can someone grab customer-impact?
elena_pm: customers reporting degraded search relevance in a few accounts, Support ticket queue has 12 mentions, some escalated. No major data loss reported.
luis_support: confirming — 3 high-severity tickets flagged, customers see timeouts and repeated partial responses. Adding affected org IDs to ticket threads.
jane_sre: joining bridge. initial guess: upstream cache eviction + retry storm causing connections to saturate. Looking at pod restarts and 429s.
ryan_oncall: mitigation step 1: scale embeddings-service to +30% capacity, apply temp circuit-breaker on downstream reranker to reduce retries. Executing now:
```
kubectl scale deployment embeddings-service -n prod --replicas=13
# apply circuit-breaker flag to reranker
curl -X POST https://ops-config/prod/flags -d '{"reranker_circuit": "trip"}'
```
ryan_oncall: scaling looks good, CPU up but health checks pass. retry rate dropping but 500s still present.
jane_sre: confirmed 500-> 200 transition window, but we still see backlog in the KV store. Tracing shows a small set of keys with very heavy hot reads (prefix collisions).
alice_eng: adding short-term mitigation: add per-key rate limit at the service layer and enable prefix sharding for the hot keys. Will push a small patch to roll out canary.
alice_eng: patch pushed to canary namespace, config snippet:
```
# per-key rate limiter
rate_limit:
  mode: key_shard
  limits:
    - keys: ["org:1234:embeds:*"]
      qps: 20
```
ryan_oncall: good. canary looks stable for 8m, promoting to 30% traffic. Observability shows error-rate trending down.
elena_pm: communicating to affected customers: we told them we have mitigation in place and are monitoring. No ETA for full root cause.
luis_support: posting status update in customer threads now. Will escalate to account execs for top-2 orgs.
jane_sre: starting timeline for post-incident review — we need to capture: alert routing config, SLO revisions, and the KV sharding fallback as an action item.
ryan_oncall: handoff to next oncall in 2h. @jane_sre can you own the hot-key RCA and action items? I can draft the incident summary and immediate mitigation steps.
jane_sre: I can own RCA. Assigning action items: [1] update paging rules to add cascade detection, [2] reduce noise by suppressing low-signal retries, [3] add hotspot alerts on KV key-level latencies, [4] schedule postmortem meeting.
elena_pm: schedule request: prefer tomorrow 1600 UTC for postmortem with Eng, SRE, Support, and PMs. I'll send calendar invite and include the affected customer list and message history.
alice_eng: technical action item: implement per-key rate limiter permanently + auto-sharding flag. ETA: 2 weeks for initial rollout, PRs will include tests and canary plan.
luis_support: follow-up: update customer comms template and log all ticket IDs into the postmortem doc.
jane_sre: alerting follow-ups (short):
- create an aggregated "alert cascade" rule that triggers when >=3 distinct services have >x error-rate in 5m
- set pager severity to S1 for cascades, but add auto-suppress for single-service flaps to cut noise
- add SLO budget check integration so we can see when mitigations are required before customer impact
ryan_oncall: noting owners: alert cascade rule -> jane_sre, suppress flaps -> alice_eng, SLO integration -> elena_pm. I'll mark these in the incident tracker.
jane_sre: also adding monitoring playbook entries: how to quickly identify hot key patterns via traces + kv metrics query examples. Example query to add to runbook:
```
# Hot key check
sum(rate(kv_gets_total{namespace="prod",key=~"org:.*"}[1m])) by (key) | topk(20)
```
elena_pm: please also add a short customer-facing timeline draft. I'll review and send.
ryan_oncall: logging this thread to incident tracker and creating a placeholder postmortem doc: https://docs/internal/incidents/1842507890. Postmortem owner: jane_sre.
luis_support: closing customer tickets as mitigated where applicable, keeping 3 tickets open for follow-up.
jane_sre: last note before handoff: schedule postmortem + action tracking sheet in the doc. I'll run RCA and share draft in 48h. Thanks team — good quick mitigation. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: issue status changed -> mitigated. Pager cleared at 16:15 UTC. Postmortem scheduled (tentative) 2026-03-17 16:00 UTC.
